QF.id: Evaluating Fund Performance and Fund Selection_32

question.text: An active equity fund returned 15% while its benchmark Nifty 50 returned 12%. What can be said about the fund manager's performance?

answer.text: The fund outperformed the benchmark by 3 percentage points
The fund underperformed because 15% is less than expected
Benchmark comparison is not relevant for active funds
The fund manager took no active decisions

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says an active fund is expected to outdo its benchmark, so fund performance is compared against the benchmark return. Here, 15% (fund) - 12% (benchmark) = 3 percentage points of outperformance over the benchmark. The Trap: The other options either misread 15% versus 12%, claim benchmark comparison is not relevant for active funds, or wrongly assume no active decisions were taken. Note: Benchmark comparison is the source-backed way to read this kind of result; over time, consistent under-performance versus benchmark would weaken the case for an active fund.
